reason: I already pay a freelancer who knows my clients and gets things done; I'm not handing my customer emails to an AI I've never seen work, and I don't have the evenings to set it up and babysit it. 59 a month isn't the problem, my time and my reputation are.
objection: If the AI answers a customer wrong or sends something odd, it's my name on it, and I'll spend more time checking it than the freelancer costs me. And what is a 'credit' anyway, 100 a month sounds like it runs out fast.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing it handle my own real customer emails for a couple of weeks on the free plan, set up by their team, with me approving every reply from my phone, and clearly fewer hours than my freelancer bills.
